title: Improve PitchDetector (autocorrelation/FFT) or scope as crude
description:
Improve PitchDetector (src/nodes/pitch.rs:184) or honestly scope it as crude. Today it is a zero-crossing detector that mis-tracks harmonic-rich signals (reports 2x fundamental) and has no confidence output. Replace with a windowed autocorrelation detector (handles harmonics, RT-safe, fixed window, no per-block alloc) or, if scoped minimal, document the limitation and tighten the test to pure tones only.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW `pitch_detector_sine`: 440 Hz sine → ~440 Hz (±5%).
3. NEW `pitch_detector_harmonic`: saw/triangle at 220 Hz → detects ~220 Hz fundamental (autocorrelation); if scoped crude, replace with pure-tone-only assertion + doc comment.
4. Output finite, no NaN/Inf.

## Design
A. Add fixed-length ring buffer to PitchDetectorState.
B. Each block push samples; compute normalized autocorrelation over lags [50Hz..8kHz]; pick first peak → freq = sr/lag.
C. Smooth/hold estimate; emit on output port. Prefer autocorrelation.
D. Add tests. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Add a ring buffer of fixed length (e.g., 2048) to PitchDetectorState.
B. Each block, push samples; compute normalized autocorrelation over lags [min..max] corresponding to [50 Hz..8 kHz]; pick first peak after the zero lag; freq = sample_rate / lag.
C. Smooth/hold the estimate across blocks (state.period replaced by lag history); emit the estimate on the output port.
D. If choosing "crude scope", instead add a doc comment "zero-crossing; pure tones only" and keep tests to sine only. Prefer the autocorrelation implementation.
E. Add `#[cfg(test)]`; iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-dsp -- -D warnings` clean.
2. NEW test `pitch_detector_sine`: 440 Hz sine → output converges to ~440 Hz (±5%).
3. NEW test `pitch_detector_harmonic`: saw/triangle at 220 Hz → detects ~220 Hz fundamental (not 440), proving autocorrelation; if scoped as crude, this test is replaced by a documented pure-tone-only assertion + a code comment stating the limitation.
4. Output finite, no NaN/Inf.

title: Add stereo FX and missing filter features (stereo reverb, resonant drive, PEQ, 1-pole util, clamp ladder cutoff)
description:
Add missing real-world FX/filter features: a true stereo reverb, a parametric EQ (PEQ), a 1-pole utility filter, resonant drive on the SVF, and a clamped ladder cutoff. Today fx.rs/utility.rs are mono-only and there is no PEQ or 1-pole node; LadderFilter (filters.rs:217) uses `fc = cutoff/sample_rate` with no clamp (unstable at high cutoff), and SvfFilter has no drive stage.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW `StereoReverb` (fx.rs): 2 in / 2 out, decorrelated delays. Test: L/R impulse responses correlation < 0.5 AND mono input produces L==R.
3. NEW `ParametricEq` (biquad peaking): at center frequency gain applied within ±1 dB; test with a sine at center freq.
4. NEW `OnePole` (lowpass/highpass): -3 dB at cutoff within ±1 dB; stable step response.
5. LadderFilter cutoff clamped to `min(cutoff, sample_rate*0.45)`: test feeds cutoff=1e6 Hz and asserts all finite (no NaN/Inf).
6. SvfFilter gains `drive` field with tanh saturation: test asserts higher drive increases THD vs drive=1.0, still finite.

## Design
A. fx.rs: add `StereoReverb` (two SimpleReverb with slightly different comb lengths per channel).
B. filters.rs: add `ParametricEq` (BiquadFilter peaking; coeffs from frequency/gain/Q) and `OnePole` (y = y + a*(x-y)); add `drive: f32` to SvfFilter applying `tanh(out*drive)`.
C. LadderFilter: `cutoff = cutoff.min(sample_rate*0.45).max(10.0)` per sample.
D. Add the six `#[cfg(test)]` tests; render via loops + FFT/RMS/finite checks. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. fx.rs: add `StereoReverb` (two SimpleReverb instances with slightly different comb lengths per channel to decorrelate; shared or per-channel mix).
B. filters.rs: add `ParametricEq` (BiquadFilter peaking sections; compute coeffs from frequency/gain/Q in init_state or set_param) and `OnePole` (y = y + a*(x-y), a from cutoff in [0,1)). Add `drive: f32` to SvfFilter and apply `out = tanh(out*drive)` before assigning output[i].
C. filters.rs LadderFilter: `let cutoff = cutoff.min(sample_rate*0.45).max(10.0);` at top of the per-sample loop.
D. Add the six `#[cfg(test)]` tests in fx.rs/filters.rs; render via local block loops and assert with FFT/RMS or finite checks.
E. Run cargo test/clippy; iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-dsp -- -D warnings` clean.
2. NEW `StereoReverb` node (src/nodes/fx.rs): 2 input ports / 2 output ports, per-channel reverb with decorrelated delays. Test: L and R impulse responses have correlation < 0.5 (decorrelated) AND a mono input produces identical L==R (no false stereo).
3. NEW `ParametricEq` node (biquad peaking, reuse BiquadFilter math): at center frequency the gain is applied within ±1 dB of `gain` dB; test with a sine at the center freq.
4. NEW `OnePole` node (lowpass/highpass): -3 dB at cutoff within ±1 dB (sine sweep test); stable step response.
5. LadderFilter cutoff clamped to `min(cutoff, sample_rate*0.45)`: NEW test feeds cutoff=1e6 Hz and asserts `output.iter().all(|x| x.is_finite())` (no NaN/Inf).
6. SvfFilter gains a `drive` field with tanh saturation: NEW test asserts higher drive increases THD (harmonic energy) vs drive=1.0, still finite.

title: Replace toy PitchShifter with a proper algorithm or scope as basic
description:
Replace the toy PitchShifter (src/nodes/pitch.rs:14) with a correct, honest algorithm. Today it computes `delay_samples = sample_rate/440/ratio` — hard-codes A4 and does not actually resample, producing a broken pitch effect. Replace with a proper time-domain varispeed pitch shifter (fractional read pointer + linear interpolation) and document its honest scope (transposes pitch, stretches time).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW `pitch_shift_up`: 440 Hz sine, shift=+12 → ~880 Hz (FFT within 5%).
3. NEW `pitch_shift_down`: shift=-12 → ~220 Hz.
4. NEW `pitch_shift_finite`: output finite, peak gain < 2x input.
5. Doc comment states it is a varispeed (transposition + time-stretch) shifter.

## Design
A. Rewrite PitchShifterState to hold a ring buffer + `read_pos: f32` + `index`.
B. process_block: `ratio = 2^(shift/12)`; write input at `index`, read via `helpers::linear_interpolate` at `read_pos`, advance `read_pos += ratio`, wrap; advance `index`. Dry/wet mix.
C. Keep ports. Add the four tests; iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Rewrite PitchShifterState to hold a ring buffer `Vec<f32>` + `read_pos: f32` + `index`.
B. In process_block: `ratio = 2.0f32.powf(shift/12.0)`; each sample write input into ring at `index`, read from `read_pos` via `helpers::linear_interpolate(&ring, read_pos)`, advance `read_pos += ratio` and wrap; advance `index`. Mix dry/wet with `mix`.
C. Keep input ports (input, shift_mod, mix_mod) and PortId mapping.
D. Add the four `#[cfg(test)]` tests; render via local loop. Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-dsp -- -D warnings` clean.
2. NEW test `pitch_shift_up`: 440 Hz sine in, shift=+12 semitones → output fundamental ~880 Hz (FFT within 5%).
3. NEW test `pitch_shift_down`: shift=-12 → ~220 Hz.
4. NEW test `pitch_shift_finite`: output finite (no NaN/Inf) and peak gain < 2x input.
5. Doc comment on PitchShifter states it is a varispeed (transposition + time-stretch) shifter, not a time-preserving one.

title: Defensive outputs indexing in Constant and Lfo (use get_mut(0))
description:
Harden defensive output indexing in Constant (oscillators.rs:526) and Lfo (nodes/lfo.rs). Both index `outputs[0]` directly, which panics if the runtime supplies an empty output slice. Switch to `outputs.get_mut(0)` with an early return so a mis-wired graph fails silently instead of panicking inside the RT callback.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW `constant_no_panic_empty_outputs`: call Constant::process_block with `&mut [Vec::<f32>::new()]`; assert no panic.
3. NEW `lfo_no_panic_empty_outputs`: same for Lfo.
4. No `outputs[0]` (unchecked) remains in those two process_block bodies (grep check).

## Design
A. Constant: `let Some(output) = outputs.get_mut(0) else { return; };`.
B. Lfo: same guard.
C. Add the two tests. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. In Constant::process_block, replace `let output = &mut outputs[0]; for sample in output...` with `let Some(output) = outputs.get_mut(0) else { return; }; ...`.
B. In Lfo::process_block, apply the same `get_mut(0)` guard at the start.
C. Add the two `#[cfg(test)]` tests; iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-dsp -- -D warnings` clean.
2. NEW test `constant_no_panic_empty_outputs`: call Constant::process_block directly with `&mut [Vec::<f32>::new()]` (zero outputs); assert it returns without panicking.
3. NEW test `lfo_no_panic_empty_outputs`: same for Lfo.
4. No `outputs[0]` (unchecked) remains in those two process_block bodies (grep check).

title: Harden RT test to a true zero-alloc assertion or document why not
description:
Harden the RT-safety story for auxide-dsp: today there is no real zero-allocation proof for process_block, only claims. Add a true per-block zero-alloc assertion (custom GlobalAlloc counter in tests, dhat is already a dev-dep) for representative nodes, and explicitly document any node that must allocate (ConvolutionReverb allocates only in init_state, not per block).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW `process_block_zero_alloc`: install a counting GlobalAlloc shim; for SvfFilter, AdsrEnvelope, Delay, SawOsc run `process_block` for several blocks and assert 0 bytes allocated during the block loop.
3. ConvolutionReverb documented that allocations happen only in init_state; process_block alloc-free (probe or `#[ignore]` test + doc note).
4. Any node that cannot be made alloc-free gets a documented reason.

## Design
A. Add a test-only `CountingAlloc` (GlobalAlloc wrapper) + thread-local byte counter in `#[cfg(test)]`.
B. Wrap process_block between counter snapshot/restore; assert delta==0.
C. For ConvolutionReverb, assert init_state allocates but process_block does not; add doc comment.
D. Fix any accidental per-block allocs. Iterate.

PLAN:

B. Wrap process_block calls between counter snapshot/restore; assert delta==0.

title: Add anti-aliasing: PolyBLEP to Triangle/Pulse; interpolation to WavetableOsc
description:
Add band-limited generation to TriangleOsc and PulseOsc via PolyBLEP, and linear interpolation to WavetableOsc. Today (src/nodes/oscillators.rs) only SawOsc (line 114) and SquareOsc (lines 158-161) call `crate::helpers::polyblep`; TriangleOsc (line 190) and PulseOsc (line 233) emit raw discontinuities, and WavetableOsc (line 292) truncates phase to the nearest table index with `table[idx]`. Goal: every periodic oscillator is alias-free and the wavetable reads smoothly.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green.
2. NEW `polyblep_triangle_bandlimited`: render TriangleOsc 1 s at 8 kHz / 44.1 kHz, FFT, assert energy in bins above Nyquist is >= 40 dB below the fundamental (vs a truncation reference).
3. NEW `polyblep_pulse_no_aliasing`: PulseOsc pw=0.1 at 8 kHz, same >40 dB below-fundamental criterion.
4. NEW `wavetable_interpolates`: WavetableOsc over a smooth ramp at a non-integer frequency; max |out[i]-out[i-1]| smaller than truncation reference AND interpolated output differs from `table[floor(phase*len)]` by > 1e-3 somewhere.
5. `cargo clippy -p auxide-dsp -- -D warnings` clean.

## Design
A. helpers.rs already exports `polyblep` and `linear_interpolate` — reuse.
B. TriangleOsc: compute band-limited square via polyblep and accumulate (add state) to get triangle; replace the sin(|saw|...) formula; keep phase wrap.
C. PulseOsc: generalize SquareOsc polyblep (edges at 0 and pw) — add the two corrections currently missing.
D. WavetableOsc: replace truncation with `linear_interpolate(&table, state.phase * len)`.
E. Add the four tests; run test+clippy; iterate.
design:
PLAN (definitive beats):
A. helpers.rs already exports `polyblep(phase, phase_inc)` and `linear_interpolate(buffer, read_pos)` — reuse, no new helpers needed.
B. TriangleOsc: a triangle is the integral of a band-limited square. In process_block, compute band-limited square `sq = 2*polyblep(phase,inc) - 1.0` style and accumulate into a `tri_state` (add field to OscState or new state). Scale so peak ~1.0; replace the current `sin(|saw|...)` formula. Keep phase wrap.
C. PulseOsc: generalize the SquareOsc polyblep logic (edges at phase=0 and phase=pw) — it already clamps pw; just add the two `polyblep` corrections currently missing (only SquareOsc has them).
D. WavetableOsc: replace `let idx = (state.phase*len) as usize % len; *sample = table[idx];` with `let read_pos = state.phase * (len as f32); *sample = crate::helpers::linear_interpolate(&table, read_pos);`.
E. Add the four `#[cfg(test)]` tests above inside oscillators.rs; render via `auxide::rt::render_offline` or a local loop at block 64.
F. Run `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` and `cargo clippy -p auxide-dsp -- -D warnings`; iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold before close:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green.
2. NEW test `polyblep_triangle_bandlimited`: render TriangleOsc 1 s at 8 kHz / 44.1 kHz, FFT the buffer, assert energy in bins above Nyquist (>= 22050 Hz) is >= 40 dB below the fundamental bin (aliasing suppressed vs. a truncation reference).
3. NEW test `polyblep_pulse_no_aliasing`: PulseOsc pw=0.1 at 8 kHz, assert same >40 dB below-fundamental criterion on above-Nyquist bins.
4. NEW test `wavetable_interpolates`: WavetableOsc over a smooth ramp table at a non-integer frequency; assert max |out[i]-out[i-1]| (continuity) is smaller than the truncation reference AND interpolated output differs from `table[floor(phase*len)]` by > 1e-3 somewhere (proves interpolation active).
5. `cargo clippy -p auxide-dsp -- -D warnings` clean.

title: Make SynthBuilder and EffectsChainBuilder actually connect nodes
description:
Make SynthBuilder and EffectsChainBuilder (src/builders.rs) actually connect nodes with edges. Today they only call `graph.add_external_node` with no edge wiring, so the produced graph is disconnected (no path to OutputSink) and cannot make sound. Add fluent auto-chaining that wires output port 0 of each added node into input port 0 of the next, and connects the head to OutputSink.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW `synth_builder_connects`: SynthBuilder osc+SvfFilter+AdsrEnvelope+build(64) compiles and produces non-zero output (proves osc→filter→env→sink wiring).
3. NEW `effects_chain_runs`: EffectsChainBuilder add_input().add_effect(Delay).add_output(); feed impulse at Dummy input, assert output equals known delayed impulse.
4. Graph edge count == (nodes - 1) and there is a path from first node to OutputSink.

## Design
A. Track `last_node` in each builder; `add_*` returns self after wiring `last_node:0 -> new:0`.
B. `add_input` adds Dummy+sets last; `add_output` adds OutputSink and wires `last:0 -> sink:0`.
C. Provide chain helper if needed. Add tests driving RuntimeCore/render_offline. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Track `last_node: Option<NodeId>` in each builder. `add_oscillator/add_filter/add_envelope/add_effect` returns `self` after recording the new node id and, if `last_node` set, adding an edge `last_node:0 -> new:0` (Rate::Audio). `add_input` adds a Dummy and sets last_node. `add_output` adds OutputSink and wires `last_node:0 -> sink:0`.
B. `build`/`build_graph` unchanged (compile final graph).
C. Provide an `fn chain<T>(mut self, node:T) -> Self` helper if needed for explicit chaining.
D. Add the `#[cfg(test)]` tests building + running via RuntimeCore or render_offline; iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-dsp -- -D warnings` clean.
2. NEW test `synth_builder_connects`: `SynthBuilder::new().add_oscillator(SawOsc).add_filter(SvfFilter).add_envelope(AdsrEnvelope).build(64)` yields a graph that compiles and, when run, produces non-zero output (proves osc→filter→env→sink wiring).
3. NEW test `effects_chain_runs`: `EffectsChainBuilder::new().add_input().add_effect(Delay{delay_ms:..}).add_output().build(64)`; feed an impulse at the Dummy input, assert output equals the known delayed impulse.
4. Graph edge count equals (nodes - 1) and there is a path from first node to OutputSink (assert `graph.edges.len()` and that every non-sink node has an outgoing edge).

title: Fix misnamed SpectralGate (rename or implement real spectral gating)
description:
Fix the misnamed SpectralGate (src/nodes/pitch.rs:106). It is actually a time-domain envelope-follower noise gate, not a spectral (FFT) gate. 3. NEW `noise_gate_silences_below_threshold`: input RMS below `threshold` → output ≈0; above → passes.
4. No remaining `impl`/public reference to the old misnomer without the alias.

## Design
A. Rename struct + impl + State in pitch.rs.
B. Add `#[deprecated] pub type SpectralGate = NoiseGate;` and `NoiseGateState` alias.
C. Add `#[cfg(test)] noise_gate_silences_below_threshold`. Iterate.

title: Add an IR loader for ConvolutionReverb
description:
Add an impulse-response (IR) loader for ConvolutionReverb (src/nodes/fx.rs:638). The node already does FFT convolution from an in-memory `ir: Vec<f32>`, but there is no way to load an IR from a WAV file or generate one programmatically. Add `from_wav(path)` (via hound) and an in-memory exponential-decay IR generator.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW `ir_from_wav`: write a short WAV (hound, dev-dep), load via `from_wav`, feed impulse, assert output tail matches IR shape (decays toward 0).
3. NEW `generated_ir`: `from_exponential_decay(0.5, sr)`; impulse yields output longer than input (reverb tail) and finite.
4. Doc states IR-length → FFT-size relationship.

## Design
A. Add `hound` to dev-deps.
B. `impl ConvolutionReverb { from_wav(path) -> Result<...>; from_exponential_decay(decay_s, sr) -> Self { ir = exp(-t/decay) } }`.
C. Keep existing `ir` field. Add tests. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Add `hound` to `[dev-dependencies]` of auxide-dsp (already a dependency of auxide, safe to reuse).
B. Add `impl ConvolutionReverb { pub fn from_wav(path) -> Result<Self, anyhow-ish/Box<dyn Error>> { read hound, collect f32 samples, Self{ir, mix:1.0} } pub fn from_exponential_decay(decay_s, sr) -> Self { build ir = exp(-t/decay) over ~decay*1.5 s } }`.
C. Keep existing `ir` field construction path.
D. Add the `#[cfg(test)]` tests; iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-dsp -- -D warnings` clean.

3. NEW test `generated_ir`: `ConvolutionReverb::from_exponential_decay(0.5, sample_rate)`; feeding an impulse yields an output longer than the input (reverb tail present) and finite.
4. Document the IR-length → FFT-size relationship (`fft_size = (ir_len+block_size-1).next_power_of_two()`) in the node doc.

title: Add voice/polyphony and note-on/off to envelope gate helper abstraction
description:
Add a reusable voice/polyphony helper that maps MIDI-style note-on/off + velocity + pitch onto the existing envelope-gate + oscillator nodes, giving a musician-friendly `Voice`/`PolySynth` abstraction built ONLY from current NodeDef nodes (no new DSP). The midi crate's voice_state.rs tracks ADSR stages but produces no audio; this bead puts a working, testable voice in auxide-dsp so the midi synth path can be wired to real sound.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW module `auxide_dsp::voices` exporting `Voice` and `PolySynth` (N voices, simple allocator). `Voice::note_on(midi_note, velocity)` sets oscillator frequency (note_to_freq) and triggers its AdsrEnvelope gate; `note_off` releases.
3. NEW test `voice_note_on_produces_sound`: after note_on, sum voice output through a mixer to OutputSink, run blocks, assert non-zero, rises then holds, after note_off falls to ~0 within release_ms.
4. NEW test `voice_pitch`: note_on(69) fundamental ~440 Hz; note_on(81) ~880 Hz.
5. `PolySynth` 8 voices: 8 distinct notes → 8 active; 9th steals oldest.

## Design
A. Create src/voices.rs; `pub mod voices;` in lib.rs.
B. `Voice` owns `Box<dyn NodeDefDyn>` osc + env + gain; per block run env with constant gate (1.0 while held), then osc, multiply by env*velocity.
C. `PolySynth` holds `[Voice; 8]` + allocator; `note_on/note_off/process(&mut [f32])` summing active voices.
D. Add `#[cfg(test)]` driving Voice/PolySynth directly with in-memory buffers. Iterate.

Per `process_block`, run env with a constant gate buffer (1.0 while held, 0.0 on release), then run osc, then multiply osc output by env level * velocity_gain into the voice's output buffer.

E. Iterate until cargo test/clippy green.

title: Add correctness and golden tests for filters and envelopes
description:
Add correctness and golden tests for filters and envelopes. Today src/nodes/filters.rs and src/nodes/envelopes.rs have zero golden/spec tests; behavior (cutoff accuracy, envelope timing, ladder self-oscillation) is unverified. Pin down the spec with measurable tests.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; clippy clean.
2. NEW `biquad_lowpass_3db_at_cutoff`: sine at cutoff → output RMS within 1 dB of input/√2.
3. NEW `svf_lowpass_3db_at_cutoff`: same for SvfFilter Lowpass.
4. NEW `adsr_timing`: A=10ms,D=10ms,S=0.7,R=10ms @44.1k; after A+D level≈0.7±0.1; after note-off+R, level≈0.
5. NEW `ladder_self_oscillation`: resonance>0.9, silent input → bounded oscillation (finite, non-zero), proving self-oscillation.

## Design
A. Add `#[cfg(test)]` modules to filters.rs/envelopes.rs.
B. Render via local helper (build node, init_state, feed constant/sine for N blocks).
C. Use helpers + block math. For self-osc, run ~1 s silence, assert finite + non-zero. Iterate.
design:
PLAN:

B. Render via a local helper: build node, init_state, feed a constant or sine buffer for N blocks, inspect outputs.

title: Define parameter surfaces for controllable external nodes
description:
Define and implement the live parameter surface for every controllable external node. The kernel contract lives in src/control.rs: canonical indices PARAM_FREQUENCY=0, PARAM_CUTOFF=1, PARAM_RESONANCE=2, PARAM_WAVEFORM=3, PARAM_DETUNE=4, PARAM_PAN=5. RuntimeCore::apply_control_msg (auxide/src/rt.rs) routes SetFrequency/SetFilterCutoff/SetFilterResonance/SetDetune/SetWaveform/SetPan onto external nodes by calling NodeDef::set_param with these indices, and TriggerGate/AllNotesOff onto NodeDef::gate. Today almost no auxide-dsp node implements set_param or gate, so MIDI/RT control is a no-op. Goal: every node with a meaningful live param implements set_param (mapping canonical indices → live state), and every envelope implements gate.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide-dsp` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide-dsp -- -D warnings` clean.
2. Oscillators SawOsc/SquareOsc/TriangleOsc/PulseOsc/WavetableOsc/SuperSaw and filters SvfFilter/LadderFilter implement `set_param` honoring PARAM_FREQUENCY/PARAM_CUTOFF/PARAM_RESONANCE/PARAM_DETUNE/PARAM_WAVEFORM where applicable.
3. AdsrEnvelope/ArEnvelope/AdEnvelope implement `gate` so TriggerGate{on:true} begins attack and TriggerGate{on:false} begins release.
4. NEW test `param_surface_roundtrip`: for each listed node, build via Graph + RuntimeCore::new_with_channels, send the relevant ControlMsg variants, run one block, and assert the live value took effect (observable: e.g., SvfFilter cutoff shift moves spectral centroid; oscillator freq change moves zero-crossing rate; envelope gate makes level rise then fall). At least one observable assertion per node type.
5. NEW test `envelope_gate_live`: TriggerGate on → level rises within A ms; TriggerGate off → level falls to ~0 within R ms.

## Design
A. KEY CONSTRAINT: `set_param(&self, state, ...)` receives immutable `self`, so live values MUST live in `State`, not in the node fields. Add live-override fields to each State struct. `self` holds the *default*; `process_block` reads `state.live.unwrap_or(self.field)`.
B. Implement `set_param` on each oscillator/filter writing the matching canonical index into State. Map PARAM_WAVEFORM for nodes that have a mode field.
C. Implement `gate` on the three envelopes toggling Attack/Release phase.
D. Add a helper `fn live_or<T>(state_val: Option<T>, default: T) -> T` in helpers.rs.
E. Add the `#[cfg(test)]` tests; drive with RuntimeCore + control.send(...). Iterate until all green.
